messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: psi in data augmentation with subpopulations
parts:
Dear all,

I have a Q on data augmentation in an occupancy model with subpopulations.

I am helping some otter biologists here in Switzerland better understand their spraint (= crap) surveys in terms of detection probability. One data set is from a tripled survey with an expert, a trained volunteer, and a search dog doing the same stretch of river one after the other and recording every spraint found. This is repeated in two winters and then they are interested in contrasting p among 4 mutually exclusive river 'naturalness categories'. Hence, I am fitting a closed-population  model implemented as an occupancy model, where I distinguish 8 subpopulations (winter x category), for which I do separate DA. (I know I could do the Royle, Link, Converse ~ 2012 thing but that hurts my brain more so I do it the pedestrian and clumsy way.)

Now I am a little lost in seeing the difference between a model that has a single DA parameter psi and one for which psi is different for each subpopulation. Here are the estimates of spraint population sizes (NU) per subpopulation in a model with a single psi (psi and constant p also shown):

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: psi in data augmentation with subpopulations
parts:
I definitely think the latter is better, allowing psi to vary by subpopulation.  Suppose you could make it hierarchical too, given the 8 subpopulations.

One analogy is a closed capture-recapture model with sex.  The proper approach is either you fix the sex for your augmented individuals and allow sex-specific psi (psi_f, psi_m), or you could have a single psi and sex is assigned a probability distribution (pr_m) for the augmented individuals.  In either case, you are estimating 2 probabilities.  If you kept a single probability for psi and fixed the sex for the augmented individuals with no probability distribution, you are constraining the model in a potentially undesirable way.

Admittedly, I'm shooting from the hip here... :)

I definitely think the latter is better, allowing psi to vary by subpopulation.  Suppose you could make it hierarchical too, given the 8 subpopulations.

One analogy is a closed capture-recapture model with sex.  The proper approach is either you fix the sex for your augmented individuals and allow sex-specific psi (psi_f, psi_m), or you could have a single psi and sex is assigned a probability distribution (pr_m) for the augmented individuals.  In either case, you are estimating 2 probabilities.  If you kept a single probability for psi and fixed the sex for the augmented individuals with no probability distribution, you are constraining the model in a potentially undesirable way.

Admittedly, I'm shooting from the hip here... :)

Hey Marc, I think the major difference is that the variances of the population sizes are forced to be essentially the same with a single psi.  If you allow psi to vary by subpopulation, the variance scales more with population size.

On Fri, May 13, 2022 at 8:41 AM Marc Kery <marc...@vogelwarte.ch> wrote:
Dear all,

I have a Q on data augmentation in an occupancy model with subpopulations.

I am helping some otter biologists here in Switzerland better understand their spraint (= crap) surveys in terms of detection probability. One data set is from a tripled survey with an expert, a trained volunteer, and a search dog doing the same stretch of river one after the other and recording every spraint found. This is repeated in two winters and then they are interested in contrasting p among 4 mutually exclusive river 'naturalness categories'. Hence, I am fitting a closed-population  model implemented as an occupancy model, where I distinguish 8 subpopulations (winter x category), for which I do separate DA.
